findings.title: Monitor context returns raw config, not the copy with the humanized schedule_type
findings.body: `get_monitor_environment_context` copies `monitor.config` into `config` and replaces `schedule_type` with `get_schedule_type_display()`. It then returns `monitor_environment.monitor.config` instead of `config`, so the conversion is discarded. The occurrence's monitor context therefore carries the raw integer schedule_type rather than the display label. This was carried over unchanged from `mark_failed.py`, but the move into a new module is a good time to fix it by returning `config`.

findings.title: Renamed/moved helpers drop the old import paths with no compatibility aliases
findings.body:
These names are no longer available from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed`:
- `mark_failed_threshold` is now `incidents.try_incident_threshold`.
- `create_issue_platform_occurrence` is now `incident_occurrence.create_incident_occurrence`.
- `get_failure_reason`, `get_monitor_environment_context` and `SimpleCheckIn` have moved to other modules.

No re-exports or aliases are left behind, and no test files were updated in this PR. Any test that patches `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed.<name>` or imports these helpers from `mark_failed` will fail with AttributeError or ImportError, and so will other modules or getsentry code that do the same. Either update those references or keep temporary re-exports in `mark_failed.py`.
